doc.title: Luis Conte interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 24, 2025

chapter: Life as a session and touring musician
title: Hit songs worth telling the family: Clapton, Colbie Caillat, Irakere
summary: Conte recalls overdubbing Clapton's Change the World with Babyface, knowing Colbie Caillat's Bubbly would be a hit, and being called to replace Irakere's conga player.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: After you did like a couple of hundred studio dates I’m guessing that you stopped reporting on every one of them when you got home. I mean here in Central New York we don’t – if you do a studio date it’s sort of an event. And you come home and sort of say, “Hey how did it go.” What would really make you bring this up, what your date was like today to your wife or your kids. This was significant? What kind of date?

If I played on a song, if this is a record and I played on a song that I thought was really going to be a hit then I’d mention. I remember I played on an Eric Clapton song, it was called “Change the World” I think that was the name, “Change the World.” It was a hit. © Fillius Jazz Archive -15-

And I remember going in, and the producer was Babyface. And I went to overdub. They already had – JR had played drums, Paul Jackson Jr., Eric was going to come in and play the guitar. And here’s an example of a great producer. Babyface would come in, says, “Hey check it out. Listen to the song.” He goes, “You know what to do.” So I went in there and did my thing. But the song was so great, I came home and I went like, “I think I just played on a hit song.” Eric Clapton. Okay. And another time it was, this is a more modern, it’s a girl, Colbie Caillat is her name. There’s a song called “Bubbly.” It was a huge hit when my daughter was just getting out of high school. And the weird thing was like I knew that song was going to be a hit. I could feel it. And I went in and I just mentioned it to my wife, “Hey I played with this girl, Colbie Caillat man.” And my daughter goes, “Colbie Caillat! She went to high school with me.” I go, “Really?” She said, “Yes.” “Well I did a song that’s going to be a hit.” And it was. But that’s rarely. I don’t talk much about it. If it’s like some, like Chucho Valdes came to town and I just played with him then I’d be talking about it. I’d be going, “Man I just played” I just played, and Irakere came (when Irakere was together) to play here in L.A. and the conga player did not get a visa. And they called me. I couldn’t believe it. I was like what? You want to hear what happened? I’ll tell you real quick. I was doing actually, they called me up and it was a show they were doing at UCLA. And I was actually in the daytime I had to do, I was working on a record with Sheryl Crow, who was another big star, right, and Hugh Padgham and them, and they says, “You’re going to get there by 6 o’clock, the show is at 8. I says, “Okay, yeah, I can get there” because the session usually goes until 5. But of course it’s a record so it’s not really going just right and I just went – at 5 o’clock I went like, “Hugh, I’m sorry Bro, I’ve gotta go. I’ll be back tomorrow.” He says okay, you know, blah-blah-blah. So I get over there and I’m so excited because Irakere man, I mean. And those guys are like backstage and I walk in and I was – I must have sounded like I was a groupie man, because I’m going like “Chucho, man I listened to this song, man I love you guys man,” this and that blah-blah-blah. Carlos DelPuerto, Emilio, and blah-blah-blah-blah-blah. And they was looking at me like okay. So no rehearsal, they had already sound checked. So I go up there and I started playing. The first song they played is “Mambo Influenciado.” And Chucho goes, “Hey when there’s a break coming up, you know, I’ll give you – just keep your eyes open you know.” “Yeah, cool.” I know all their tunes, man. So the song – we finished it, boom I nailed everything. Chucho stops the show and goes like – he stands up and looks at me and he goes like, “Hey, all that stuff that you were saying is true.” I’ll never forget that. But stuff like that, man, I would talk about that all day. © Fillius Jazz Archive -16-
